newsitem.title: UK: Highland whisky sees improving U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Highland whisky sees improving U.S. market.

text.p: Whisky-maker Highland Distilleries Plc, maker of Famous Grouse blend, said Tuesday that the market for spirits in North America has finally turned a corner after a decade in the doldrums.
But it said conditions in Britain remain very difficult, with sales volumes continuing to contract.
The company reported a 12 percent increase in its pre-tax profit for the half-year to Feb. 28 to 24.9 million pounds ($40.6 million), in line with market forecasts.

It included for the first time prestigious single malt whisky producer Macallan-Glenlivet for a full period. Macallan posted a profit of 5.0 million pounds ($8.1 million), but this was offset by the cost of financing the acquisition, which produced an interest bill of two million pounds ($3.3 million).
A rise in the value of the pound adversely affected Highland's results by around one million pounds ($1.6 million).
Sales overseas of the Famous Grouse grew 5 percent in the six month period, the company said.
The main increases were in Greece, Holland and Sweden, while France was disappointing. But exports to North America and Asia showed strong growth.
In Britain industry sales were down 5 percent in the period.

In North America, exports of Famous Grouse rose 19 percent and sales of single malt Macallan were up 20 percent, the strongest increase in sales to the region for a decade, said Chief Executive Brian Ivory.

"I think the market for spirits in North America probably has turned a corner, but how sharp the corner and how steep the trend I am not sure. Certainly the demand for Scotch and the image of Scotch has improved. It is now considered a prestigious product again."
Ivory said the company expects to achieve an overall 1997 price increase of about 2 percent on its brands overseas.
